title: September 11 Attacks: Factual Overview
content: The September 11 attacks (often referred to as 9/11) were a series of four coordinated terrorist attacks by the militant terrorist group al-Qaeda against the United States on September 11, 2001. The attacks occurred in the United States, specifically in New York City and Washington, D.C. Four commercial airplanes were hijacked by 19 al-Qaeda terrorists. Two planes struck the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center in New York City, causing both towers to collapse. A third plane hit the Pentagon in Washington, D.C. The fourth plane, United Airlines Flight 93, crashed near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, after passengers and crew members attempted to retake control of the aircraft. The attacks did not occur in India or any other country outside the United States. Nearly 3,000 people were killed in the attacks, making it the deadliest terrorist attack in human history. The 9/11 attacks took place in the United States, with the primary targets being in New York City and Washington, D.C.
